title: Area XII review: Postflight Procedures
intro: These 20 questions cover Area XII's one Task, After Landing, Parking, and Securing. They follow a flight from the rollout to the tie-down, then the write-ups and records that come after.

questions.q: You land at a towered airport with one passenger and will leave the airplane overnight. Which plan follows the AFH from rollout to walking away?
options: Raise the flaps on the rollout, stop just past the runway edge, then taxi in and shut down from memory
Taxi past the hold lines, park, let your passenger climb out while the propeller winds down, then shut down and tie down
Stop past the hold lines and do the after-landing checklist, park, shut down with the checklist, then leave the walkaround for the next pilot's preflight
Stop past the hold lines and do the after-landing checklist, park, shut down with the checklist, let your passenger out, walk around the airplane, then tie down and lock it
questions.why: Do the after-landing checklist after a complete stop past the holding position markings [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]. Shut down with the POH checklist. After shutdown and deplaning, do a postflight walkaround, then tie down, secure the controls and lock up [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. Nobody gets out while the propeller turns, because a spinning propeller can kill [[24:53|AFH 2-16]].

questions.q: You land on Runway 27 at a towered airport and turn off onto Taxiway C. Right after C's hold lines, Taxiway C meets parallel Taxiway A. The tower has given no other instructions. If you stop before Taxiway A, your tail will still be short of the hold lines. What should you do?
options: Stop before Taxiway A; a tail a few feet short of the lines is fine
Keep going until the whole airplane is past the hold lines, even if the nose pokes into Taxiway A, then hold
Turn onto Taxiway A and taxi to the ramp, since you are off the runway
Stop on the runway and ask the tower where to go
questions.why: With no ATC instructions, taxi past the runway holding position markings even if that means sticking into or crossing another taxiway or ramp. Once every part of the airplane has crossed them, hold unless ATC says more. At a towered airport, don't stop on the runway without ATC approval [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

questions.q: During your flight the oil temperature gauge read zero the whole time, and you write it up after landing. The school airplane has an air-cooled engine and no MEL. Can the next pilot defer it with an INOPERATIVE placard for a day VFR flight?
options: No. It is required equipment for day VFR, so this kind of deferral can't be used
Yes, if a pilot decides it is not a hazard and placards it
Yes, but only until the next annual inspection
Yes, as long as the oil pressure gauge still works
questions.why: An oil temperature gauge for each air-cooled engine is required for day VFR [[60:486|14 CFR 91.205(b)]]. The 91.213(d) deferral can't be used for items required by 91.205 [[60:493|14 CFR 91.213(d)]]. Put the write-up in the maintenance or discrepancy record so it gets fixed [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]].

questions.q: In a typical piston trainer shutdown, which control actually stops the engine, and when does the ignition switch go to OFF?
options: The ignition switch stops it; then the mixture goes to idle cutoff
The mixture at idle cutoff stops it; the ignition switch goes OFF once the engine has stopped
The master switch stops it; then the ignition switch goes OFF
The throttle at idle stops it; the ignition switch goes OFF before the mixture
questions.why: The AFH shutdown list sets the mixture to IDLE CUTOFF, then turns the ignition switch OFF when the engine stops. The only earlier use of the switch is a quick check at idle that the magnetos ground in OFF [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

questions.q: You park at a large airline airport you have never visited. You can't tell which parts of the ramp are inside the SIDA. What does the AIM suggest?
options: Assume the whole ramp is open to pilots and their passengers
Walk wherever the airline workers walk
Contact the airport authority; airports with a SIDA have a description and map of its boundaries
Stay by your airplane until a TSA officer comes to you
questions.why: If you are unsure where a SIDA is, contact the airport authority. Airports with a SIDA have a description and map of its boundaries. Moving into a SIDA without authorization and displayed ID is prohibited [[33:173|AIM 2-3-15]].

questions.q: You land at a non-towered airport. Your taxi route to parking crosses another runway. What should you do before you cross it?
options: Listen on the CTAF and scan the whole runway, including its approach and departure paths, since not every airplane has a radio
Cross right away, since you just landed and know the pattern is empty
Call ground control for a crossing clearance
Turn on the landing light and cross, since landing airplanes must yield to taxiing ones
questions.why: After landing at a non-towered airport, remember not all aircraft have radios. Before entering or crossing a runway, listen on the CTAF and scan the full length of the runway, including its approach and departure paths [[7:7|AC 91-73B]]. Without an operating tower, you must make sure of separation before crossing the hold lines [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5]].

questions.q: On your postflight walkaround you find a wet streak of fluid running down from the right brake. The brakes felt normal on the rollout. What should you do?
options: Wipe it off; the brakes worked, so it isn't worth reporting
Write it up in the maintenance or discrepancy record so it gets checked and repaired
As a student pilot, remove the wheel fairing and tighten the fitting yourself
Report it only if it is still there before your next flight
questions.why: The postflight walkaround checks the brakes for leaking hydraulic fluid [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. Record it in the maintenance or discrepancy record [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]]. The owner or operator must have discrepancies repaired, and can only do that if you report them [[60:520|14 CFR 91.405]].

questions.q: After a lesson the dipstick shows 4 quarts. Your POH says to keep 6 to 8 quarts. What should happen before you leave the airplane?
options: Nothing; oil only needs checking during the next preflight
Add oil well above 8 quarts so it lasts longer
Leave it, since the engine ran fine at 4 quarts
Bring the oil up to the POH level (or have line service do it) and record the servicing
questions.why: Postflight, check the oil and bring it to the AFM/POH level [[24:60|AFH 2-23]]. The ACS also asks you to document servicing needs, so note it on the squawk sheet or record the school uses.

questions.q: You fly a retractable-gear airplane. Its POH says to raise the flaps during the rollout after a short-field landing to help braking. What must you do before you move the flap control?
options: Positively identify the flap handle, so you don't raise the landing gear by mistake
Wait until you are at the parking spot
Ask the tower for approval
Turn the master switch off
questions.why: When the maker calls for flaps up on the rollout, positively identify the flap control first. Pilots have raised the landing gear instead of the flaps while the airplane was still moving [[24:59|AFH 2-22]] [[24:181|AFH 9-10]].

questions.q: You finish a lesson with the tanks half full. Another student takes the airplane in an hour for a short local flight, and full tanks would put her over maximum weight. How should the airplane be fueled now?
options: Fill both tanks to the top; full tanks are always best after a flight
Fill only the left tank so she can choose
Add fuel based on what the next flight needs, from its flight planning
Leave it; fuel is never part of the postflight
questions.why: Add fuel based on the airplane's next use. If another flight is planned, fuel for that flight's planning needs. Filling the tanks to stop condensation is for an airplane that will sit unused [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

questions.q: You land on Runway 28L at a towered airport. The exit taxiway is short, and the hold lines for parallel Runway 28R come right after 28L's hold lines. You can't get your tail past 28L's markings without crossing 28R's. What should you do?
options: Cross 28R's hold lines; leaving a runway never needs a clearance
Stop with your tail over 28L's markings and wait quietly for ground
Turn around on 28L and use a different exit
Stop and tell ATC right away
questions.why: If an adjacent parallel runway's hold short line keeps you from clearing the landing runway, stop and immediately advise ATC [[7:7|AC 91-73B]]. Don't enter another runway, or stop or reverse course on a runway at a towered airport, without ATC approval [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

questions.q: Years from now you hold a private pilot certificate and own a small airplane. You change the oil yourself, which is allowed preventive maintenance. What must your maintenance record entry include?
options: Only the date and the tach time
A description of the work, the date, and your name, signature, certificate number and kind of certificate
Nothing, if a mechanic will look at it during the next annual
Only a note on the airplane's squawk sheet
questions.why: A pilot who does preventive maintenance must make an entry in the maintenance record with a description of the work, the date, and the pilot's name, signature, certificate number and type of certificate [[1:240|PHAK 9-10]] [[60:132|14 CFR 43.9(a)]]. At least a private pilot certificate is needed to approve the return to service [[60:132|14 CFR 43.7(f)]].

questions.q: Strong wind is forecast overnight. Your tie-down spot has worn ropes at the wings and a chain at the tail. Which setup matches the AFH?
options: Cinch the ropes reasonably snug, leave a little slack in the chain, and install the control lock and rudder gust lock
Pull the chain as tight as it goes and leave the ropes loose
Skip the control lock, since the ropes hold the airplane still
Leave every tie loose so the airplane can turn into the wind
questions.why: Ropes are flexible and may be cinched reasonably to the tie-down rings. Chains don't stretch, so leave some movement to avoid airframe damage. Secure the flight controls, and consider a rudder gust lock and covers [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

questions.q: You land a little long. At the first taxiway you are still rolling at about 35 knots. The next taxiway is 1,500 feet ahead. What is the best choice?
options: Make the turn anyway, since it is the first taxiway
Stay on the centerline, slow to normal taxi speed, and exit at the next taxiway
Stop on the runway and turn around back to the first taxiway
Turn onto the grass beside the runway to clear quickly
questions.why: Slow to normal taxi speed before turning off. A sharp turn at higher speed can damage the gear, tires, brakes or structure [[24:59|AFH 2-22]]. At a towered airport, don't stop or reverse course on the runway without ATC approval [[33:264|AIM 4-3-21]].

questions.q: You stop for fuel on a two-leg trip. On the rollout the left brake felt soft, and on the walkaround you find brake fluid dripping from that wheel. Your passenger says, "We only need brakes to taxi, let's go." What is right?
options: Continue; brakes aren't used in flight
Continue, then write it up when you get home
As PIC you decide if the airplane is safe; with a leaking brake, don't fly the next leg until it is checked and repaired
Let the passenger decide, since it is a shared trip
questions.why: The pilot in command decides whether the airplane is in condition for safe flight [[60:436|14 CFR 91.7]]. Leaking brake fluid is exactly what the walkaround looks for [[24:60|AFH 2-23]], and discrepancies must be repaired [[60:520|14 CFR 91.405]].

questions.q: You are checking out in an airplane with a turbocharged engine and a constant-speed propeller. Which shutdown items from the AFH list apply to it that a basic trainer doesn't have?
options: Propeller control to low rpm, then a short run at high power
None; skip the checklist, since its steps are for basic trainers
Mixture full rich, and skip the magneto check
Follow the maker's turbo spool-down procedure, and set the propeller control to high rpm
questions.why: The AFH shutdown list says to follow the maker's spool-down procedure if turbocharged, and to set the propeller control to HIGH rpm if equipped. Always use the airplane's own POH checklist [[24:60|AFH 2-23]].

questions.q: During shutdown, a lineman knocks on the window to ask about fuel. Afterward you can't remember whether you turned off the avionics and the alternator. What should you do?
options: Assume you did, since you always do them in the same order
Turn the master switch on and off again to be safe
Go back to the shutdown checklist and confirm each item
Leave it for the next pilot's preflight
questions.why: A checklist is a memory aid that keeps critical items from being forgotten. You can do the steps and then use the list to confirm them. Pilots who rely only on memory become complacent [[24:36|AFH 1-15]]. Distractions push out other tasks [[24:51|AFH 2-14]].

questions.q: After you shut down, a line worker grabs a propeller blade to turn it so the tow bar fits better. What does the AFH say about touching a propeller?
options: Always assume the ignition is on; a faulty switch can let the engine start
It is safe once the master switch is off
It is safe as long as the ignition key is out
It is only risky while the engine is still hot
questions.why: While touching a propeller, always assume the ignition is on. A faulty magneto switch can be OFF and still let the engine start [[24:53|AFH 2-16]]. A broken ground wire plus leftover fuel in a cylinder can start the engine when the prop is moved [[1:176|PHAK 7-16]].

questions.q: Why must the whole airplane, tail included, be past the runway holding position markings when you exit, and not just the main wheels?
options: So the tower can read your tail number
Because the transponder must be set to standby there
The markings generally mark the edge of the runway safety area, and you aren't clear of the runway until every part has crossed them
Because ground control can't hear you on the runway side of the lines
questions.why: Runway holding position markings generally mark the boundary of the runway safety area. An airplane exiting a runway isn't clear until all of it has crossed them [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5]]. Make sure the tail section is across too [[7:7|AC 91-73B]].

questions.q: Last week you wrote up a soft brake. The school says a mechanic replaced the brake parts. Before you fly the airplane, what must be true?
options: The mechanic told the front desk; nothing needs to be written
Your CFI taxied it around the ramp
Your squawk has been crossed off the squawk sheet
A maintenance record entry was made and an authorized person approved the airplane for return to service
questions.why: No one may operate an aircraft after maintenance unless an authorized person has approved it for return to service and the maintenance record entry has been made [[60:521|14 CFR 91.407(a)]]. The owner or operator must make sure those entries are made [[60:521|14 CFR 91.405(b)]].
